correctness.rationale: Complete 0-, 1-, 2- and 3-coordinate support enumeration of F^{-1}(0) in the nonnegative octant. The 3x3 circulant determinant equals (1+alpha+beta)D with D=((alpha-1)^2+(beta-1)^2+(alpha-beta)^2)/2. All finitely many zero roots for alpha,beta!=1 have nonzero Jacobian; axial omitted-coordinate multipliers are (R+1)(1-alpha),(R+1)(1-beta), and face omitted-coordinate multiplier (R+1)D/(1-alpha beta). Their exact signs give the 8-vs-2 local positive sheet count. All positive preimages of u>0 satisfy p_i<h, making their collection compactly bounded; any unlisted roots as u->0 would accumulate at an already enumerated zero root, contrary to IFT uniqueness. Singular alpha=beta=1 case reduces exactly to q^2-(R+1)q+R sum(u)=0. Exact rational arithmetic and finite Newton diagnostics passed; diagnostics do not replace these arguments.

originality.rationale: The originating 2024 full text states the three-dimensional map and raises noninvertibility, but its studied bifurcations and its model discussion do not imply or state the 8-to-2 local positive inverse-sheet dichotomy. The 2010 three-dimensional Lotka-Volterra paper explains generic inverse and critical-set geometry and treats a different asymmetric case with predominantly planar computations; it neither gives the present model-specific support enumeration nor the sign/compactness argument. A 2001 planar paper and indexed same-family periodic-bifurcation results likewise do not cover the claim. An unindexed broad polynomial inverse theorem is the residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible literature on multivariate quadratic cyclic map inverse multiplicity may imply the exact same classification.

value.rationale: The extinction observation and its neighborhood are canonical backward-reconstruction targets in a studied noninvertible ecological map. The theorem completely classifies the one-step positive inverse multiplicity throughout two open parameter regimes with a sharp threshold at unit competitive strength. The strong-competition paradox—eight nonnegative zero ancestors but only two strictly positive ancestors of every sufficiently small positive observation—is a concrete boundary-versus-interior structural transition; it is not a generic reparametrization or merely a computed Jacobian sign. The result gives a precise inverse-valence boundary pertinent to studying basin folding, while explicitly limiting itself to one-step local observations.
